'''Paul Anthony Keddy''' (born May 29, 1953 in [[London, Ontario]]) was a Canadian [[ecologist]]. He studied plant [[population ecology]] and [[community ecology]] in [[wetland]]s and many other habitats in eastern Canada and [[Louisiana]], United States.

He began his formal training in [[biology]] in 1969 at [[York University]] in [[Toronto]] and finished his [[PhD]] at [[Dalhousie University]] with [[E. C. Pielou|Evelyn C. Pielou]]. He was a professor of [[biology]] for 30 years, first at the [[University of Guelph]] (1978–1982), then the [[University of Ottawa]] (1982–1999) and then held the ''Edward G. Schlieder Endowed Chair for Environmental Studies'' at [[Southeastern Louisiana University]] (1999 to 2007). He published over 150 scholarly articles, wrote seven books, and edited two books. He was designated a Highly Cited Researcher by Clarivate (formerly the Institute for Scientific Information).,<ref>[https://clarivate.com/highly-cited-researchers/past-lists/ Clarivate Highly Cited Researchers]</ref> He received the National Wetlands Award for Science Research in 2007<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eli.org/national-wetlands-awards/paul-keddy|title = Homepage &#124; ELI National Wetlands Awards}}</ref> from the [[Environmental Law Institute]]. Although he worked on many types of plant communities and a broad array of ecological questions, the focus of his work was on the principles that organize plant communities, with particular emphasis upon wetlands.

==Books==
Synthesis was one of Paul Keddy's major contributions to wetland ecology and [[plant ecology]]. His first book, ''Competition'',<ref>Keddy, P.A. 1989. ''Competition''. (Population and Community Biology Series). Chapman & Hall, 202 p.</ref><ref name="Sterner 1991 pp. 225–226">{{cite journal | last=Sterner | first=Robert W. | title=Review of ''Competition'' by Paul A. Keddy | journal=The Quarterly Review of Biology | publisher=University of Chicago Press | volume=66 | issue=2 | year=1991 | issn=0033-5770 | doi=10.1086/417207 | pages=225–226}}</ref> won both the [[George Lawson Medal]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cba-abc.ca/AwardRes.htm |title=Home |access-date=2008-06-27 |archive-date=2008-02-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080211110423/http://www.cba-abc.ca/AwardRes.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> of the [[Canadian Botanical Association]] and the [[Henry Allan Gleason Award]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.botany.org/awards_grants/detail/gleason.php |title=Henry Allan Gleason Award |access-date=12 March 2012 |archive-date=11 March 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120311012449/http://www.botany.org/awards_grants/detail/gleason.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> of the [[New York Botanical Garden]]. A second edition of ''Competition'' was published in 2001.<ref>Keddy, P.A. 2001. ''Competition''. 2nd edn. Kluwer, 552 p. {{ISBN|978-1-4020-0229-8}} [https://www.springer.com/life+sciences/evolutionary+%26+developmental+biology/book/978-0-7923-6064-3?changeHeader]</ref>

A major area of research for Keddy, ecological [[assembly rules]] (the constraints (rules) on community formation and maintenance (assembly), was the topic of his co-edited synthesis ''Ecological Assembly Rules: Perspectives, Advances, Retreats''.<ref>Weiher, E. & Keddy, P. (1999) ''Ecological Assembly Rules: Perspectives, Advances, Retreats''. Cambridge University Press, 430 p. {{ISBN|978-0-521-65235-3}} [https://books.google.com/books?id=RIZDYJ0zKaAC]</ref>

In 2006 Keddy was honoured by the [[Society of Wetland Scientists]] with the Merit Award for ''Wetland Ecology: Principles and Conservation''.<ref>Keddy, P.A. 2000. Wetland Ecology: Principles and Conservation. Cambridge University Press, 614 p. {{ISBN|0-521-78367-4}} [https://books.google.com/books?id=0QwMcXzHeMoC Google books]</ref> A new edition of ''Wetland Ecology''<ref>Keddy, P.A. 2010. ''Wetland Ecology: Principles and Conservation''. Cambridge University Press, 497 p. {{ISBN|9780521519403}} [http://www.cambridge.org/ca/knowledge/isbn/item5708528/Wetland%20Ecology/?site_locale=en_CA]</ref> was published in 2010.<ref name="Smardon 2014 pp. 813–817">{{cite journal | last=Smardon | first=Richard | title=Review of ''Wetland Ecology Principles and Conservation'', 2nd edition, by Paul Keddy | journal=Water | publisher=MDPI AG | volume=6 | issue=4 | date=2014-04-02 | issn=2073-4441 | doi=10.3390/w6040813 | pages=813–817| doi-access=free }}</ref> This textbook is used in courses around the world.  In 2005 he focused on the world's largest wetlands which had not previously been described, ranked or compared, and co-edited ''The World's Largest Wetlands: Ecology and Conservation''.<ref>Fraser, L.H. & Keddy, P.A. 2005. ''The World's Largest Wetlands: Ecology and Conservation''. Cambridge University Press, 498 p. {{ISBN|978-0-521-83404-9}}</ref>

In 2007, he published ''Plants and Vegetation: Origins, Processes, Consequences'',<ref>Keddy, P.A. 2007. ''Plants and Vegetation: Origins, Processes, Consequences''. Cambridge University Press, 680 p. {{ISBN|978-0-521-86480-0}} [http://www.cambridge.org/features/biology/keddy/]</ref> a textbook on plant ecology.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Review of ''Plants and Vegetation: Origins, Processes, Consequences'' by Paul A. Keddy|author=Bond, William|journal=BioScience|year=2009|volume=59|issue=8|page= 713|doi=10.1525/bio.2009.59.8.18|s2cid=130818562 }}</ref>

His later books for [[Cambridge University]] Press included Plant Ecology (2017), A Framework for Community Ecology (2021), and a third edition of Wetland Ecology: Principles and Conservation (2023).<ref>{{cite web |title=Wetland Ecology: Principles and Conservation (3rd edition) |website=Cambridge University Press |url=https://www.cambridge.org/highereducation/books/wetland-ecology/BEEFD81EE59AEDFF1198ADBBC647632C |access-date=2026-09-29}}</ref><ref name="ESA2024"/>

In addition to scientific writing, Keddy prepared guides to the natural history of two regions of North America. For the [[State of Louisiana]] he authored ''Water, Earth, Fire: Louisiana's Natural Heritage''.<ref>Keddy, P.A. 2008. ''Water, Earth, Fire: Louisiana's Natural Heritage''. Xlibris, Philadelphia. 229 p.</ref> For [[Lanark County]], Ontario, he wrote ''Earth, Water, Fire: An Ecological Profile of Lanark County''.<ref>Keddy, P.A. 2008. ''Earth, Water, Fire: An Ecological Profile of Lanark County''. Motion Creative Printing (revised first edition 1999), 73p.</ref>  For this contribution Keddy was given a Champion of Nature Award (2008) by the Mississippi Valley Field Naturalists<ref>''The Lanark Era.'' 2008. Champions for Nature are honoured by Mississippi Valley Field Naturalists. May 27, p. 4</ref> and the Lanark County Award of Excellence—Heritage and Ecology by the county (2009).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.county.lanark.on.ca/Page1671.aspx |title=2009 Recipients |website=www.county.lanark.on.ca |access-date=22 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517054712/http://www.county.lanark.on.ca/Page1671.aspx |archive-date=17 May 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
